name: Mango
description: An operator-managed newsletter with consent-aware audience imports, hosted signup, email authoring, exact-revision approval, and provider-confirmed delivery reporting.
scope: One self-hosted newsletter and its equal operators. Mail is required; commerce, SMS, and AI are optional. Wider commerce and multichannel contract clauses remain release obligations.

capabilities.description: A static, hand-illustrated public landing page at `/` for the newsletter profile: Mango's mark and name, a hero, how a letter leaves Mango, consent, approval of the exact letter, scheduling, delivery reports, ownership and a closing call to action, linking to sign-in and the first-party docs, with the owner's configured name, one-line description and optional credit in the footer. It reads no record or session, sets no cookie, and loads only same-origin fonts, styles, scripts and favicons.

First-party public documentation at `/docs` for the people who run Mango: the repository Markdown that `docs/site.json` publishes, rendered to HTML at build time by a Vite plugin and served per request inside the public landing's shared header and footer, cookie-free and same-origin, describing the default newsletter profile only.

Base sessions and confirmed invitations, equal product powers, retained attribution, initial self-removal and last-active-operator protection; Local hosted acceptance proved mailed sign-in and native-session access on one disposable workers.dev installation, with no production authentication claim.
Imports customers, products, orders, refunds, carts, and browsing events from one connected commerce store, tracks per-source freshness, and blocks approval on stale or missing sources.
Tracks each contact's independent per-channel consent state, evidence, opt-outs, imports, merges, dormancy, and erasure with a surviving opt-out record.
Generates ranked, evidence-cited campaign proposals from store data with grounded AI content and honest forecast provenance, held as drafts until an operator approves a revision.
Resolves and rechecks campaign audiences against consent, commerce, dormancy, and frequency rules, freezing the candidate set at approval and re-excluding at dispatch.

Operator-authored blank and recorded-signal drafts without AI, shared proposal Review, rich/HTML content with managed footer and plain text, structured live audience counts, store-zone scheduling, exact-revision approval and existing cancellation/test-send controls.
Enforces sender identity, authentication, unsubscribe and opt-out mechanics, link and content checks, personalisation fallbacks, and sending-reputation limits before any send.

Hands recipient-steps to email and SMS providers under their declared retry guarantees, reconciles unknown outcomes where evidence is available, throttles retry-safe transport failures, and pauses a channel during a provider outage; SendGrid uses at-most-once handoff and operator-reviewed uncertainty.
Reports campaign history, engagement, attribution, cost, tracked-link activity, and deliverability without presenting forecasts as facts.
Exports every contact, source record, consent record, campaign, and audit entry as JSON alongside uploaded campaign assets.

nonGoals: Store transactional messaging (order, shipping, and account notifications)

externals.why: Mango needs the buyer's real customers, products, carts, browsing signals, orders, refunds, and inventory to identify and recheck opportunities.
data: Webhook acknowledgements sent back to the store confirming receipt of an event
Explicit adapter requests for source records (customers, products, orders, refunds, carts, browsing events)

externals.why: A language model turns structured evidence into reviewable campaign content and explanations; Cloudflare primitives do not provide that model capability.
data: The proposal evidence required for the requested generation
The configured business context required for the requested generation

externals.why: Internet email delivery, domain authentication, bounce handling, and complaint feedback require a delivery provider with established sending infrastructure.
data: Operator email addresses that receive magic links, test sends, and dispatch-paused notices

externals.why: Registered sending numbers, carrier routing, country approval, compliance keywords, and delivery receipts require a telecommunications provider.
A public DNS-over-HTTPS resolver verifies that each approved external link and redirect target resolves outside private networks before dispatch.

operatingCost.assumptions: One store, 10000 contacts, 4 campaigns per month, 20000 email and 5000 SMS recipient-steps, and 500 AI generations. Queue messages are at most 64 KB and dispatch stays below 3334 recipient-steps per UTC day.
operatingCost.cloudflareMonthlyUsd: $0 on the current Workers Free plan while the deployment stays inside every Free quota: at most 100000 dynamic Worker requests per UTC day with 10 ms CPU per invocation; 10000 Queue operations per UTC day (write, read, and delete are each one operation per 64 KB); D1 at 5 million rows read per UTC day, 100000 rows written per UTC day, and 5 GB total storage; and SQLite Durable Objects at 100000 requests and 13000 GB-s per UTC day. Workers Paid starts at $5/month and is required for the declared 100000-contact campaign: its 100000 recipient-step writes plus step and schedule mutations exceed D1 Free's 100000 rows-written-per-UTC-day limit.
operatingCost.externalMonthlyUsd: Not yet estimated because the reference commerce, email, SMS, and AI adapters have not been selected; required before first release.
operatingCost.totalMonthlyUsd: Incomplete until reference adapters and unit prices are selected.
